# py-core: PyO3 bindings core (jix-py)

## Purpose

The Python `jix.Array` (`jix-py/src/array.rs:122-130`) is a `frozen` pyclass holding a type-erased
`ArrayAny` plus a `Mutex<ArrayCache>` (cached numpy descr + one reusable `ReadContext`). This
subsystem covers materializing to numpy (`numpy()`, `__getitem__`, `out=`, `__array__`, `item`,
`plain`), basic-index parsing (`ops/shape_ops.rs:229-378`, shared with `jix.slice`), numpy <-> jix
dtype mapping (`dtype.rs`), `compact` + `resolve_array_params` (`array.rs:1712-1831`), archive
read/write incl. Python file-like adapters and mmap (`archive.rs`), helpers (`util.rs`), type-hint
wrappers (`type_hint.rs`), module registration (`lib.rs`) and the package shim
(`python/jix/__init__.py`). Wrapping numpy input zero-copy (`plain_from_numpy`,
`ops/common/operand.rs:449-520`) belongs to py-ops but is the source side of most contracts here.
The module declares free-threading support: pyo3 0.30.1 `#[pymodule]` defaults `gil_used=false`
(pyo3-macros-backend `module.rs:421`); release.yaml ships 3.14t/3.15t and 32-bit (x86, armv7,
win32) wheels. errstate/geterr were removed in #95 (no `error.rs` any more).

## Contracts

Provided to Python callers:
- `Array.numpy(index=None, *, out=None)` (`array.rs:537-659`): returns an array of the shape
  selected by `index` plus the dtype's inner dims (numpy expands a subarray descr into trailing dims
  of its base dtype, `array.rs:547-553`). Without `out`: a fresh `PyArray_Empty` allocation in the
  storage's `read_layout_order` (`array.rs:559-581`, `util.rs:143-177`), layout documented as
  implementation-defined (`array.rs:506-511`); inner dims always innermost and C-contiguous.
  With `out`: the same object, after `check_output_array` (`array.rs:213-309`): `is_equiv_to` the
  cached descr's base, exact shape, `NPY_ARRAY_WRITEABLE`, then (only if non-empty) base pointer and
  every stride of an extent>1 dim aligned to the jix dtype alignment, no negative/zero stride on
  extent>1 dims, C-contiguous inner dims, and no two elements overlapping (sorted-stride criterion,
  `array.rs:293-307`). Empty selections return before the stride rebuild (`array.rs:588-591`).
- `__getitem__(i)` == `numpy(i)` (`array.rs:741-744`). Grammar (`shape_ops.rs:229-378`): int (not
  `bool`, `shape_ops.rs:271`), `slice` with step 1, at most one `...`, tuple of these (len <= 9 incl.
  the ellipsis). Strict bounds; `start == len` / empty slices allowed (`shape_ops.rs:340-361`);
  trailing dims filled; int items drop their dim. `a.numpy(None)` reads all (pyo3 maps None to
  `Option::None`), but `a[None]` is a TypeError.
- `__array__(dtype=None, copy=None)` (`array.rs:759-783`, NEW): always copies via `numpy()`;
  `copy=False` -> ValueError; `dtype` -> `astype(dtype, copy=False)` on the fresh array.
- `item()` (`array.rs:680-688`) requires ndim 0, then numpy's `.item()`. `plain()` (`array.rs:724-738`)
  = `numpy(index)` re-wrapped by `plain_from_numpy` with the array's own jix dtype (keeps inner
  shape) and DEFAULT params, caching the same numpy descr.
- `jix.compact` (`array.rs:1712-1733`): `asarray` then `compact_with` under `py.detach`.
  `resolve_array_params` (`array.rs:1735-1831`): unknown keys -> TypeError, wrong types -> TypeError,
  unknown codec/filter and bad `read_size` arity -> ValueError; builder errors via `into_py_result`.
- `read_array` / `write_array` (`archive.rs:78-150`, `226-285`): path I/O runs detached; file-likes
  run attached through `PyReader` / `PyWriter`. `offset` and `mmap=True` only for paths. Default
  validation is core's `ArchiveValidation::default()` = Strict (`jix/src/archive/mod.rs:22-31`).
  A failed path write removes the new file or truncates an appended one back (`archive.rs:259-272`).
  A successful file-like read seeks the stream to just after the archive (`archive.rs:143-145`).
- Error mapping (`util.rs:64-100`): a `PyErr` found as the error's direct `source()` (or inside a
  direct `io::Error` source) is re-raised with its type; else `Arithmetic` -> `ArithmeticError`
  (CHANGED in #95, was FloatingPointError), `UnsupportedDtype` -> TypeError, `Io` -> OSError,
  everything else -> RuntimeError.

Relied on from jix core / py-ops:
- `Array::to_buf_strided_into` (`jix/src/array/read.rs:423-439`): validates the index
  (`check_ranges`, `jix/src/error.rs:228-250`, incl. per-dim `usize` fit), the 32-bit region size
  (`error.rs:298-312`), and the destination (`check_out_buf_impl`, `jix/src/storage/buf.rs:384-431`:
  stride count, writable, no overlap, span <= the slice the `StridedBuf` was built over). It cannot
  see the real numpy allocation: jix-py builds that slice itself (`array.rs:628-652`), so a wrong
  span is UB before core runs. Push mode must write EVERY element of the region: the fresh
  `PyArray_Empty` memory is uninitialized and handed to Python.
- `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts_mut` (`buf.rs:89-110`): valid for the span, exclusive for its
  lifetime, must not overlap memory any array in the chain reads, no aliasing strides.
- `Plain::new` (`jix/src/storage/plain.rs:66-123`): data valid for the strided span (gaps
  included, one allocation) for the storage lifetime, and NOT written while the array is read or a
  pull buffer of it is alive. jix-py keeps the ndarray alive (`operand.rs:515-517` stores
  `array.unbind()`), but cannot stop Python from writing it (other threads while detached,
  free-threaded builds, `out=` aliasing, `resize(refcheck=False)`).
- Core shapes: every dim <= i64::MAX and byte size fits u64 (`check_shape_overflow`,
  `jix/src/error.rs:192-194`). jix-py relies on it in `shape[d] as i64` (`shape_ops.rs:309,317,333,370`)
  and `size()` (`array.rs:378-380`, unchecked u64 product).
- `spec().read_layout_order()` (`jix/src/storage/params.rs:744`) is a permutation of `0..ndim`; an
  out-of-range entry panics at `array.rs:576` (`drop_dims[dim]`), a duplicate makes
  `PyArray_Transpose` raise.
- `read_from_file_mmap` (`jix/src/archive/array.rs:173-252`): UB if the file is modified while
  mapped; jix-py forwards this to users (`archive.rs:31-34`) and calls it in `unsafe` (`archive.rs:120-123`).
- `Array::read_ctx` (`jix/src/array/mod.rs:246-251`) `expect`s `ReadContext::new` (only fails if
  zstd `Decompressor::new()` fails, `jix/src/context.rs:71-81`); jix-py calls it while holding the
  cache mutex (`array.rs:166-169`), so a panic there poisons the cache for that Array.
- `Dtype::new_struct` (`jix/src/dtype.rs:569-622`) rejects padding, out-of-order/duplicate fields,
  nesting > 32, and alignments that are neither 1 nor the aligned layout. `ScalarKind::alignment`
  is hard-coded (`jix/src/dtype.rs:950-967`; 8 for i64/u64/f64, K8).

## Edge-case surface

- Zero-length: `check_output_array` returns before stride/alignment checks when the numpy shape has a
  0 (`array.rs:246-250`); `numpy()` returns at `nitems == 0` (`array.rs:588-591`). Inner dims are
  never 0 (core rejects zero inner shapes).
- 0-d: index is empty, `nitems = 1`, span = itemsize. `a[()]` / `a[...]` return a 0-d ndarray, never
  a numpy scalar. `__len__` on 0-d raises ValueError (`array.rs:394-404`). There is no `__iter__`
  or `__setitem__` (arrays are immutable, `frozen`).
- Length-1 dims: their stride is never stepped; a negative numpy stride there is replaced by the
  C-order value (`array.rs:609-622`, debug_assert only). Huge strides on length-1 dims pass through
  (`stride * 0` in the span).
- Dropped (int-indexed) dims get synthetic C-order strides (`array.rs:601-606`); read extent 1.
- Inner shape: `np_shape = out_shape ++ dtype.shape()`; allocation uses `np_dtype.base()`; outer
  strides are read from the first `out_shape.len()` numpy dims (`array.rs:598`); `itemsize` is the
  jix itemsize (base * inner product). `numpy_empty*` take up to 32 dims (`util.rs:19`).
- Bool: `dtype_to_numpy` maps `Bool8` to numpy bool (`dtype.rs:21`); bytes are copied as-is, so a
  `bool8` source with bytes 2..255 yields a numpy bool array with non-canonical bytes.
- f16 / complex: `('f',2)`, `('c',8|16)` only; longdouble / clongdouble rejected (`dtype.rs:166-176`).
- Byte order: scalar bases with `byteorder() == b'>'` are rejected, also inside subarrays and struct
  fields (recursion, `dtype.rs:141-146`). `out` with a big-endian dtype fails `is_equiv_to`.
- Struct dtypes: fields sorted by offset (`dtype.rs:215`), no padding, nesting <= 32
  (`dtype.rs:193-197`), itemsize/offsets/inner dims must fit u16 `Itemsize`, inner ndim <= 4.
  `np.dtype([])` (empty struct, itemsize 0; unlike `'V0'`, which has no fields) likely takes the
  struct branch and yields an itemsize-0 jix dtype; core rejects itemsize 0 only at storage
  construction (`jix/src/storage/params.rs:276`) - unverified, check which paths see it first.
- Alignment: unaligned numpy INPUTS are fine (Plain allows it, `plain.rs:85-89`); unaligned `out`
  is rejected (`array.rs:255-281`) though core does not need it (`read.rs:385`).
- Aliasing: `out` overlapping any numpy array in the lazy chain is documented UB
  (`array.rs:484-504`); element-disjoint but span-interleaved views (e.g. `x[:, ::2]` out,
  `x[:, 1::2]` input) still create overlapping `&mut [u8]` / `&[u8]` (K111, open).
- Python ints: index items via `extract::<i64>` - an int beyond i64 becomes a TypeError ("only
  integers, slices...") instead of numpy's IndexError; `Dim` is i32 and rejects bool
  (`type_hint.rs:94-109`); `repeats`/`offset`/`len`/`block_size`/`read_size` are u64 (negative ->
  OverflowError); `block_shape` is `Vec<u32>`, `compression_level` i32.
- 32-bit: `read_shape` is `as usize` (`array.rs:557`) but guarded: fresh allocation rejects dims >
  `npy_intp::MAX` (`util.rs:121`), `out` dims are compared against usize shapes, core `check_ranges`
  re-checks. `slice_unpack` raises IndexError for any slice on a dim > `Py_ssize_t::MAX`
  (`util.rs:26-30`). `PyMemoryView_FromMemory(buf.len() as Py_ssize_t)` cannot wrap (slices <= isize::MAX).
  i686 Linux: numpy aligns int64/float64/complex128 to 4, jix to 8 -> `dtype_to_numpy` raises its
  layout-mismatch ValueError (`dtype.rs:75-82`) and debug builds trip `dtype.rs:222` (K8, open).
- GIL: `numpy()` stays attached only for `plain_read` storages with <= 4096 bytes
  (`array.rs:639-640`); `compact` and path read/write always detach; file-like I/O stays attached
  but runs arbitrary Python (`read`/`write`/`seek`/`tell`/`flush`) mid-read.
- mmap: unlink is fine on POSIX; truncation -> SIGBUS (UB, documented). `write_array` without
  `append` uses `create_new` (`archive.rs:244`) so it cannot clobber a mapped file; `append=True`
  to a mapped file only grows it, but a failed append calls `set_len(original)`.

## Intentional behaviors (do not report)

- `out` sharing memory with any numpy array in the chain is UB by contract (`array.rs:484-504`, K31).
- Index grammar: strict bounds, step 1 only, no None/newaxis/fancy/bool indexing, bool rejected
  (`array.rs:458-472`, `docs/module.md:92-93`, `test_getitem.py:176-210`, `test_slice.py`).
- `numpy()` layout follows the source's memory order (`array.rs:506-511`,
  `test_getitem.py:151`); `out` may be any non-reversed, non-broadcast, non-overlapping, aligned view
  (`array.rs:478-482`, `test_numpy_out.py:250-290`); a reversed length-1 out dim is accepted
  (`test_getitem.py:140`); `out` must be aligned although core does not need it.
- Negative-stride numpy inputs raise ValueError, except on dims of length <= 1 and on empty arrays
  (`operand.rs:499-509`, `array.rs:1684-1686`, K80/K141 fixed).
- Big-endian numpy dtypes raise ValueError (`dtype.rs:141-146`); structured dtypes with padding
  raise (`test_struct_dtype.py`); unsupported kinds O/U/S/M/m/V raise "Unsupported dtype"
  (`test_bad_input.py`).
- numpy bool arrays with any byte values are wrapped zero-copy as `bool8`, non-zero = True
  (`test_array_ops.py:140-147`).
- Integer division/remainder by zero and negative integer powers raise `ArithmeticError` (not
  ZeroDivisionError) when read; float ops never raise or warn (`test_arithmetic_errors.py:1-6`,
  `jix/src/error.rs:313-326`). A dtype mismatch raises TypeError; other core errors RuntimeError.
- `__bool__` always raises (`array.rs:412-417`); `__pos__` rejects bool/struct (`array.rs:1063-1076`);
  `pow(a, b, mod)` raises NotImplementedError (`array.rs:1027-1031`); `item()` only for ndim 0;
  `__len__` of 0-d is ValueError, of a dim > usize is OverflowError (K112 fixed).
- `__array_ufunc__ = None` (`array.rs:1605-1608`): numpy ufuncs on a jix Array raise TypeError, a
  numpy operand on the left defers to jix's reflected op. Binary dunders return NotImplemented for
  unknown operands whose type sets `__array_ufunc__ = None` (`array.rs:1833-1855`); other
  unsupported operands (None, str) still raise ValueError (K133, partly fixed).
- `__array__(copy=False)` raises ValueError (`test_array_protocol.py:31-36`).
- `read_array`: offset/mmap unsupported for file-likes (`archive.rs:128-137`); `len` for a file-like
  only bounds-checks (`archive.rs:29-30`); `write_array` without `append` fails if the file exists
  (`test_archive.py:44`); `append` ignored for file-likes; an append-mode file object raises after
  the bytes are written (`jix/src/archive/block.rs:237-243`, `test_archive.py:102`).
- `write()` returning None counts as a full write; `read()` returning None is EOF; over-reporting
  raises; seek returning None falls back to tell (`archive.rs:347-365,380-384,481-490`,
  `test_archive.py` "unusual writer" tests). A memoryview kept by `write()` raises
  RuntimeError "kept a reference" (`test_archive.py:117-125`); the buffer is read-only and released
  after `write()` (`test_archive.py:127-140`).
- Python exceptions from file-likes keep their type (`test_bad_input.py` `_interrupt` tests); a
  missing file with `len=` raises plain OSError (K130 remainder).
- Aliases `jix.pow/abs/concat/clip/prod/sub/mul/div/neg/log2/log10` shadow builtins on purpose and
  are listed in `__all__` (`python/jix/__init__.py:8-60`).
- `plain()` uses default params, not the source's (`array.rs:732`).

## Hot spots

New or changed since 6dbeb15 (the next hunt concentrates on these):
- NEW `__array__` (`array.rs:759-783`): numpy may call it positionally (`__array__(dtype)`) or with
  `copy=True`; is any combination returning something other than a fresh ndarray? Its docstring
  promises "the same shape as self" - false for inner-shape dtypes (trailing inner dims).
- CHANGED (#104) `numpy()` now writes through `to_buf_strided_into` (`array.rs:641-656`). Core's
  new `check_out_buf_impl` compares the region span with the slice jix-py built from the SAME
  strides, so it can only catch overlap, never a slice longer than the numpy memory. Is the rebuilt
  stride set (`597-626`) always within the allocation (dropped dims, length-1 dims with negative or
  huge strides, inner dims, transposed fresh allocation)?
- CHANGED (#95) errstate removal: `read_ctx` (`array.rs:161-174`), `compact` (`1724-1730`),
  `write_array_impl` (`archive.rs:286-297`); `ErrorKind::Arithmetic` -> `ArithmeticError`
  (`util.rs:91`). Do all read entry points still map errors through `into_py_result`? Does a
  PyErr wrapped deeper than one `source()` level lose its type?
- CHANGED (#96) `divide(rounding_mode=)`, `remainder(rounding_mode=)`, `__floordiv__`/`__mod__` use
  Floor (`array.rs:936-1014`); reflected variants swap operands - check each pair's order.
- CHANGED (#94) `resolve_array_params` builder style (`array.rs:1777-1828`): any path where an error
  is swallowed or a param silently dropped? `read_size` arity check runs before `into_dim_array`.
- MOVED `ArchiveValidation` (`archive.rs:152-177`), `ItemOrTuple` (`type_hint.rs:141-247`, logic
  unchanged), NEW `Shape` hint (`type_hint.rs:73-92`); core renames `read_from_file_with` /
  `read_from` / `write_to` (`archive.rs:116,121,140,294`); NEW `__all__` with aliases
  (`__init__.py:8-22`); lib.rs exports (`byteswap`, `isfinite/isinf/isnan`, unified divide/remainder).

Long-standing:
- `check_output_array` overlap test (`array.rs:293-307`) vs core `disjoint_span`
  (`buf.rs:398-416`): same criterion? ties, length-1 dims, inner dims.
- Cached numpy descr (`ArrayCache.numpy_dtype`) vs `arr.dtype()`: `from_core_with_np_dtype` callers
  (`as_array.rs:80`, `select.rs:92`, `shape_ops.rs:94..1220`, `array.rs:736`) cache a USER descr
  that only passed `dtype_from_numpy`, whose layout checks are debug_asserts (`dtype.rs:221-225`).
  Which descrs map to a jix dtype of different itemsize/alignment in release (K8 aside)?
- Free-threaded and detached reads: `&mut [u8]` over `out` and `&[u8]` over Plain sources live
  across `py.detach`; other threads can write, `.shape=`/`.strides=` (K152), or resize with
  `refcheck=False`. Python callbacks during file-like I/O can mutate sources mid-write: does core's
  `write_to` hold a pull view of a Plain source across `writer.write()`?
- `read_ctx` / `ContextGuard` (`array.rs:161-174,1857-1872`): re-entrancy (a `write()` callback
  reading the same Array), poisoning (`expect` under the lock), two threads swapping contexts.
- `parse_basic_index`: `-0`, huge ints, `__index__` side effects (they run before
  `check_output_array`), ellipsis plus ints filling exactly ndim, 8-dim arrays.
- `array_try_map` / `array_try_from_fn`: panic in `f` mid-way; `T` needs drop but `U` does not.
- Recent churn (`git log -15` on these files): #105 docs (`archive.rs`, `array.rs`), #104 OutBuf
  (`numpy()`), #102 View removal (`__str__`), #96 divide/remainder + test moves (most Rust tests in
  these files were deleted or moved to Python), #95 errstate removal, #94 ArrayParams builder.

  subtracting remaining buffer size...")`) when the Python `tell()` returns less than the bytes still

- [CONFIRMED in batch7-5 as K174] `jix-py/src/array.rs:754-755` - `__array__` docstring says the result has `self.shape`; for a
  dtype with an inner shape it has extra trailing dims (and `item()` at `array.rs:687` then raises
  numpy's size error for a 0-d inner-shape array, contrary to its docstring).
- [RULED OUT in batch7-5: latent only, the one panic under the lock is ZSTD_createDCtx returning NULL (OOM)] `jix-py/src/array.rs:166-169` - `self.arr.read_ctx()` (which `expect`s) runs while the cache mutex
  is held; a panic poisons it and every later `.dtype` / read of that Array raises RuntimeError
